docs.title: Swiss Travel Planner & Budget Calculator
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation for Swiss Travel Planner, an open-source, multi-AI travel calculation and itinerary generation engine.

Project Identity & Credits

  • Official Website: https://planswitzerland.com/
  • Project Owner: Plan Switzerland
  • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/swissplanner
  • License: MIT Open Source

docs.title: What is Swiss Travel Planner?
docs.text:
Swiss Travel Planner is a lightweight, high-performance web application created and owned by Plan Switzerland. It is designed to help budget-conscious travelers estimate their trip costs in Switzerland and generate personalized day-by-day itineraries.

It dynamically calculates transport pass savings (Swiss Travel Pass, Swiss Half Fare Card, Berner Oberland Pass, Tell Pass), mountain excursion fares (Gornergrat, Schilthorn, Mount Rigi, Pilatus, Grindelwald First, Jungfraujoch), budget lodging rates, daily food expenses, and live CHF to USD exchange rates.

graph TD
    User[Traveler Input] --> Form[Planner Form]
    Form --> Choice{AI Configured?}
    Choice -->|Yes| AI[Active AI Provider<br>OpenRouter / OpenAI / Groq / Ollama]
    Choice -->|No| Cache[12-Hour Pricing Cache / Built-in Fares]
    AI --> Parser[JSON Response Parser]
    Cache --> Engine[Budget Calculation Engine]
    Parser --> Engine
    Engine --> Output[Realistic Cost Breakdown & Day-by-Day Itinerary]

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 💳 Realistic Cost Calculations: Accurately computes transport passes, hostel/hotel rates, meals, and mountain excursions.
  • 🤖 Multi-AI Engine: Connects to OpenRouter, OpenAI, Groq, MiniMax, Ollama (Local AI), or any OpenAI-compatible API.
  • ⚡ Local Caching & Fallback: Stores live fare data in localStorage for 12 hours. Operates 100% offline using built-in database when no API key is set.
  • ⚙️ Centralized Configuration: All site branding, base fares, and AI presets are managed cleanly via config.js.
  • 🔐 Dual Security Modes: Choose between client-side API keys via browser modal or server-side proxy (/api/chat).
  • 🎨 Modern Design System: Built with Tailwind CSS, Lucide icons, Google Fonts (Plus Jakarta Sans, JetBrains Mono), and glassmorphism elements.

docs.title: Credits & Ownership
docs.text:
This project is created and actively maintained by Plan Switzerland, your ultimate guide for authentic, family-friendly, and budget-conscious travel in Switzerland.

  • Website: https://planswitzerland.com/
  • GitHub: https://github.com/swissplanner

docs.title: Documentation Contents
docs.text:
• Quick Start: Get up and running in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: AI Providers Integration
docs.text: Swiss Travel Planner supports any AI API compatible with the standard OpenAI /v1/chat/completions REST format.

docs.title: Supported AI Providers
docs.text: Provider Recommended Model API Endpoint URL Key Required OpenRouter google/gemini-2.5-flash https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions Yes OpenAI gpt-4o-mini https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions Yes Groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions Yes MiniMax MiniMax-M2.7 https://api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions Yes Ollama (Local) llama3.2 http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions No Custom Endpoint Any compatible model User defined URL Optional

docs.title: Method 1: Interactive Browser UI Modal (Client-Side)
docs.text:
1. Click AI Settings (⚙️) in the top header.
  2. Select your provider preset from the dropdown menu.
  3. Input your API key.
  4. Click Test Connection (⚡) to verify credentials.
  5. Click Save Settings to persist config to browser localStorage.

docs.title: Method 2: Global Preset in config.js
docs.text:
To specify a provider globally for all site visitors, edit config.js:

ai: {
  defaultProvider: "groq",
  providers: {
    groq: {
      name: "Groq",
      endpoint: "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions",
      model: "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
      requiresApiKey: true
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Method 3: Ollama Local AI Setup (100% Free & Offline)
docs.text:
You can run local AI models completely free using Ollama:

  1. Install Ollama and pull your desired model: 
    ollama run llama3.2
  2. Open AI Settings in Swiss Travel Planner.
  3. Select Ollama (Local).
  4. Endpoint: http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions
  5. Model: llama3.2
  6. API Key: (Leave blank)
  7. Click Test Connection and Save Settings.

docs.title: Response Parsing & Robustness
docs.text:
The engine handles multiple model output formats gracefully:

  • Strict JSON Object: Native JSON output via response_format: { type: 'json_object' }.
  • Markdown Codeblocks: Strips json ... formatting.
  • Reasoning Tags: Filters out <think>...</think> tags generated by reasoning models (such as DeepSeek-R1 or Qwen-QwQ).
  • Graceful Fallback: Automatically reverts to internal database if network or API errors occur.

docs.title: API Reference & Data Specs
docs.text: This page documents the API endpoints, global JavaScript configurations, and JSON data schemas used by Swiss Travel Planner.

docs.title: POST /api/chat
docs.text: Routes AI queries through a Node.js Express server or Vercel Serverless Function to fetch live transport fares and exchange rates.

docs.title: 2. Global JavaScript API (window.APP_CONFIG)
docs.text:
Access or modify the configuration programmatically via JavaScript:

// Get active branding
console.log(window.APP_CONFIG.branding.siteName); // "Swiss Travel Planner"

// Get default exchange rate
console.log(window.APP_CONFIG.defaults.chf_to_usd); // 1.10

// Inspect AI provider options
console.log(window.APP_CONFIG.ai.providers);

docs.title: 3. Browser Local Storage Keys
docs.text: Key Type Description swiss_travel_planner_ai_config JSON String Stores user-selected AI provider, endpoint, model, and API key. swiss_travel_planner_pricing_cache JSON String Cached pricing data object. swiss_travel_planner_pricing_cache_time Timestamp Epoch timestamp (ms) when cache was populated.

docs.title: Architecture & Calculation Engine
docs.text: This section explains how Swiss Travel Planner calculates budget recommendations and structures day-by-day itineraries.

docs.title: High-Level Data Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant UI as Index / Form
    participant Planner as Planner Engine (planner.js)
    participant Cache as LocalStorage Cache
    participant AI as AI Provider / API

    User->>UI: Select Travelers, Days, Season, Entry & Spots
    UI->>Planner: Submit Event Handler
    Planner->>Cache: Check Cached Pricing (12-hour TTL)
    alt Cache Miss & API Key Available
        Planner->>AI: Request Latest Prices & Exchange Rates
        AI-->>Planner: JSON Price Object
        Planner->>Cache: Store Valid JSON in Cache
    else Cache Hit or Fallback
        Cache-->>Planner: Load Baseline / Cached Fares
    end
    Planner->>Planner: Execute Budget & Hub Algorithms
    Planner-->>UI: Render Cost Breakdown Table & Itinerary Cards

docs.title: 1. Hub Selection Logic
docs.text:
Base cities are selected according to geographical hub efficiency:

  • Zermatt + Bernese Oberland: Split stays between Interlaken & Zermatt.
  • Bernese Oberland (Lauterbrunnen/Grindelwald/Interlaken): Base in Interlaken (access to budget hostels & supermarkets).
  • Lucerne: Base in Lucerne (direct connection to Mt. Rigi & Chapel Bridge).
  • Airport Arrival Hubs:
  • Zurich Airport (ZRH) -> Lucerne (45 min train).
  • Geneva Airport (GVA) -> Lausanne (30% cheaper lodging).
  • Basel Airport (BSL) -> Interlaken.

docs.title: 2. Transport Pass Optimization Algorithm
docs.text:
The engine selects the most cost-effective pass based on duration and traveler priorities:

$$\text{Short Trips } (\le 4 \text{ Days}): \text{Half Fare Card } (120 \text{ CHF}) + \text{Saver Day Passes}$$

$$\text{Medium Trips } (5\text{--}8 \text{ Days, Budget Focused}): \text{Half Fare Card } (120 \text{ CHF}) + \text{Point-to-Point Tickets}$$

$$\text{Medium Trips } (5\text{--}8 \text{ Days, Convenience Focused}): \text{Swiss Travel Pass } (3, 4, 6, \text{ or } 8 \text{ Consecutive Days})$$

$$\text{Longer Trips } (> 8 \text{ Days}): \text{Half Fare Card } (120 \text{ CHF}) + \text{Regional Pass (Berner Oberland / Tell Pass)}$$

docs.title: 3. Cost Breakdown Calculations
docs.text:
Total estimated cost ($T_{\text{CHF}}$) is computed as:

$$T_{\text{CHF}} = C_{\text{lodging}} + C_{\text{transport}} + C_{\text{food}} + C_{\text{excursions}}$$

Where: - $C_{\text{lodging}} = (\text{Rate}{\text{adult}} \cdot N}} + \text{Rate{\text{child}} \cdot N) \times (D - 1)$ - $C_{\text{transport}} = \text{PassCost}}{\text{adult}} \times N$ }(Children 6-15 get free Swiss Family Card) - $C_{\text{food}} = (35 \times N_{\text{adults}} + 20 \times N_{\text{children}}) \times D$ - $C_{\text{excursions}} = (\text{Excursion}{\text{adult}} \cdot N}} + \text{Excursion{\text{child}} \cdot N)$}

Finally converted to USD:

$$T_{\text{USD}} = \text{Math.round}(T_{\text{CHF}} \times \text{Rate}_{\text{chf_to_usd}})$$

docs.title: 4. Cache Expiration & Invalidation
docs.text:
Pricing data is cached in localStorage: - Cache Key: swiss_travel_planner_pricing_cache - Time Key: swiss_travel_planner_pricing_cache_time - TTL: 12 Hours (12 * 60 * 60 * 1000 ms)

Users can clear the cache at any time via the AI Settings modal.

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: All site settings, default pricing values, exchange rates, and AI provider configurations are centrally managed in config.js.

docs.title: Configuration Overview (config.js)
docs.text:
The configuration object is attached to window.APP_CONFIG so it is instantly available across the entire application:

window.APP_CONFIG = {
  branding: { ... },
  defaults: { ... },
  ai: { ... }
};

docs.title: 1. Branding Settings
docs.text:
Customize your site title, tagline, logo text, author name, and repository URL:

branding: {
  siteName: "Swiss Travel Planner",
  tagline: "Swiss Travel Planner & Budget Calculator",
  description: "Calculate budget estimates using Swiss Travel Pass fares, cable car prices, real-time exchange rates, and personalized day-by-day itineraries.",
  logoText: "S",
  author: "Swiss Travel Planner Team",
  repoUrl: "https://github.com/swissplanner"
}

Tip

The logoText property takes the first character to render crisp icon avatars in the header navigation and footer.

docs.title: 2. Default Pricing & Fallback Data
docs.text:
When no AI provider is configured or when offline, the calculation engine uses these baseline prices (in CHF):

defaults: {
  currency: "CHF",
  targetCurrency: "USD",
  chf_to_usd: 1.10,

  // Transport Passes (CHF)
  swiss_travel_pass: {
    "3day": 244,
    "4day": 295,
    "6day": 389,
    "8day": 429,
    "15day": 469
  },
  swiss_half_fare_card: 120,
  berner_oberland_pass: {
    "3day": 230,
    "6day": 290
  },
  tell_pass: {
    "2day": 210,
    "5day": 250
  },
  saver_day_pass_avg: 52,

  // Cable Cars & Mountain Excursion Fares (Full adult prices in CHF)
  cable_cars: {
    gornergrat: { adult: 98, child: 49 },
    schilthorn: { adult: 105, child: 53 },
    first_grindelwald: { adult: 66, child: 33 },
    rigi: { adult: 72, child: 36 },

}

docs.title: 3. AI Configuration Presets
docs.text:
Define default providers and backend proxy rules:

ai: {
  defaultProvider: "openrouter",

  providers: {
    openrouter: {
      name: "OpenRouter",
      endpoint: "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions",
      model: "google/gemini-2.5-flash",
      requiresApiKey: true
    },
    // ... additional presets
  },

  useBackendProxy: false,
  backendProxyUrl: "/api/chat"
}

docs.title: Deployment & Hosting Guide
docs.text: Swiss Travel Planner can be deployed to static web hosts, serverless platforms, Docker containers, or self-hosted Linux VPS servers.

docs.title: 1. Vercel Deployment (Recommended)
docs.text:
Vercel provides automatic serverless API routing via /api/chat.js.

  1. Fork the repository: https://github.com/swissplanner.
  2. Log into Vercel and click Add New Project.
  3. Import your forked swiss-travel-planner repo.
  4. Add environment variables in Vercel settings (optional):
  5. AI_API_KEY: Your AI Provider API Key
  6. AI_PROVIDER: openrouter (or openai, groq, minimax)
  7. AI_MODEL: google/gemini-2.5-flash
  8. Click Deploy.

docs.title: GitHub Pages (Static Mode)
docs.text:
1. In your GitHub repository settings, navigate to Pages.
  2. Set Source to Deploy from a branch -> Branch main -> / (root).
  3. Save. Your application will be live at https://<username>.github.io/swiss-travel-planner/.

docs.title: Cloudflare Pages / Netlify
docs.text:
1. Connect your GitHub repository to Cloudflare Pages or Netlify.
  2. Build command: (Leave empty)
  3. Build output directory: ./ or .

docs.title: 3. Docker Deployment (Self-Hosted VPS)
docs.text:
Deploy on any Docker host (DigitalOcean, AWS EC2, Hetzner, Linode):

  1. Build the Docker image: 

    docker build -t swiss-travel-planner .

  2. Run the container on port 80: 

    docker run -d -p 80:80 --name swiss-planner --restart unless-stopped swiss-travel-planner

docs.title: 4. Node.js Express Server on Linux (Ubuntu + Nginx)
docs.text:
1. Clone repo on your server: 

    git clone https://github.com/swissplanner.git /var/www/swiss-planner
cd /var/www/swiss-planner
npm install

  2. Setup .env configuration: 

    cp .env.example .env

  3. Manage process with PM2: 

    npm install -g pm2
pm2 start server.js --name "swiss-planner"
pm2 save

  4. Configure Nginx Reverse Proxy (/etc/nginx/sites-available/default): 

    server {
    listen 80;
    server_name yourdomain.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade';
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
    }
}

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: This guide will walk you through setting up and running Swiss Travel Planner locally or on your own server.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, make sure you have:

  • A modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge).
  • (Optional) Node.js v18+ if you want to run the Express backend proxy server.
  • (Optional) An API Key from an AI provider (e.g., OpenRouter, OpenAI, Groq, MiniMax).

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Fork and clone the repository from GitHub:

git clone https://github.com/swissplanner.git
cd swiss-travel-planner

docs.title: Option A: Static Client-Side Mode (No Installation Required)
docs.text:
Because Swiss Travel Planner is built as a zero-dependency static application, you can run it immediately without compiling code:

  1. Open index.html directly in your browser or serve it using VS Code Live Server.
  2. Click the AI Settings button (⚙️) in the top-right navigation bar.
  3. Select your preferred AI Provider, enter your API Key, and click Save Settings.

docs.title: Option B: Node.js Backend Proxy Server
docs.text:
If you want to proxy requests through a Node.js server to hide your API keys from client-side network tabs:

  1. Install project dependencies: 

    npm install

  2. Copy the environment variables template: 

    cp .env.example .env

  3. Configure your .env file: 

    PORT=3000
AI_PROVIDER=openrouter
AI_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-your-actual-api-key
AI_MODEL=google/gemini-2.5-flash
AI_ENDPOINT=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions

  4. Enable backend proxying in config.js: 

    ai: {
  useBackendProxy: true,
  backendProxyUrl: "/api/chat"
}

  5. Launch the Node.js server: 

    npm start

  6. Access the live application at http://localhost:3000.
